## RYANAIR TO CARRY ALMOST 700,000 PASSENGERS THROUGH IRISH AIRPORTS THIS OCTOBER MIDTERM


Ryanair, Europe’s No.1 airline, today (Fri, 23 Oct) announced that it expects to carry almost 700,000 passengers through its Irish airports over the October Bank Holiday and midterm break. These significant traffic figures demonstrate the continued demand for Ryanair’s unbeatable low fares, extensive route network, and industry-leading reliability, as families, friends, and holidaymakers take to the skies for an Autumn getaway.


With the October Bank Holiday and midterm offering an opportunity for a well-earned break, Ryanair customers can choose from a wide range of destinations available to book now via the Ryanair app/website.


**Ryanair’s Director of Comms, Jade Kirwan, said:**


*“We’re looking forward to welcoming almost 700,000 Ryanair passengers onboard our flights to and from Ireland this October Bank Holiday and midterm break, as our customers continue to* *enjoy Ryanair’s low fares, unrivalled route network, and industry-leading reliability for their Autumn getaways.* *”*

## [RYANAIR LAUNCHES PRAGUE – PAPHOS & KOSICE ROUTES](https://dev-corporate.fr164-0.ryanair.com/news/ryanair-launches-prague-paphos-kosice-routes/)


Ryanair, Europe’s No.1 airline, today (1st August) celebrated the first flight from Prague to Paphos, while on Monday (3rd August) it will launch a twice weekly service to Kosice, both as part of its extended Summer 2020 schedule.


To celebrate its new routes, Ryanair has launched a seat sale with fares from 729 Kc for travel to Kosice and from 759 Kc to Paphos, both until the end of October, which must be booked by Wednesday (5th August), only on the Ryanair.com website.
